prompts.description:
Author a new s0ma module end to end.

From nothing to a built, registered module: read the survival
card, then walk journey:mcp-authoring-loop — scaffold a
known-valid skeleton, edit through the check loop (diagnostics
carry the fix instructions), build, then read the module's
components back out of the self-model. The numbered steps are
rendered from that journey's record, so this prompt teaches the
path the model holds rather than a second copy of it.
prompts.name: author_module
prompts.title: Author a new s0ma module

prompts.description:
Diagnose an observed runtime fault from self-knowledge first.

Captures the symptom, orients with project_status, reads declared
runtime/runbook context, inspects suspects and dependency neighbors,
requests host evidence when applicable, then tests the smallest
hypothesis against observed behavior without reverting durable state.
prompts.name: diagnose_fault
prompts.title: Diagnose an observed runtime fault

prompts.description:
Send the user's feedback about s0ma to the s0ma team.

Identifies what is being reported, confirms it is meant for s0ma
when the user never named it, drafts from evidence alone, prepares
and shows the exact feedback data, submits only through the
client's approval form, and relays the receipt or the saved draft.
prompts.name: feedback
prompts.title: Send feedback to the s0ma team

prompts.description:
Diagnose and fix s0ma check failures until the project is clean.

Runs check for structured diagnostics, groups findings by code,
looks unfamiliar codes up in the error catalog, and applies each
diagnostic's remediation — highest severity first — re-checking
until ok.
prompts.name: fix_check_failures
prompts.title: Fix s0ma check failures

prompts.description:
Migrate a pre-consolidation project to the current s0ma surface.

Plans the migration with a migrate_ext dry run, presents the plan,
applies it (refuse-don't-clobber), rebuilds — legacy caches are
removed and the build regenerates everything — then checks until
clean.
prompts.name: migrate_project
prompts.title: Migrate a legacy s0ma project

resources.description:
Every s0ma concept, one line each.

The whole vocabulary in one read: what each word means, in the
one sentence the concept itself declares. For the full page on
any of them — what it is for, when to use it, when not to, its
syntax and what decided it — ask learn_s0ma for its id.
resources.name: docs_concepts_resource

resources.description:
What s0ma can be asked about, and how to ask.

The starting point for questions about s0ma itself rather than
about your project: every category of topic this release
documents, how many there are, an id you can copy, and the page
each category is written out on. Ask for one topic with the
learn_s0ma tool.
resources.name: docs_index_resource

resources.description:
Every worked path through s0ma, step by step.

A journey is a path from a starting point to a finished
outcome: the steps in order, what each is for, and what a good
result looks like. These are the same records the journey
prompts render, so a path read here and a path walked with a
prompt are one path.
resources.name: docs_journeys_resource

resources.description:
The s0ma diagnostic error catalog (FR-MCP-10).

Every s0ma-dsl error code in one table: severity per strictness
mode (migration / dev / strict / release) and a one-sentence
description of the cause and canonical fix. Look unfamiliar
diagnostic codes up here while working the check loop — generated
from the DSL's own error-code registry, so it cannot drift from
the diagnostics the tools return.
resources.name: errors_resource

resources.description:
What s0ma is, who it fits, and how to prove its value.

The canonical cold journey shared with the root README: initialize,
orient with project_status, inspect canonical dependency facts, watch
generated drift and pending release debt block, then explicitly prove
imports under the host application's trusted Python.
resources.name: getting_started_resource

resources.description:
The s0ma DSL patterns guide — idioms for real applications.

Worked patterns and recipes (component shapes, layering,
documentation declarations, testing) distilled from real s0ma
projects. Read after the quick reference when structuring
non-trivial modules.
resources.name: patterns_resource

resources.description:
The s0ma quick reference: every declaration, line by line.

One page, generated from the language itself when the release's
documentation is built: the kinds of declaration and when to
reach for each, every line each kind may carry and whether it
must be written, whether a line may be none or pending, the
words a line chooses from, a checked sample of every kind, the
everyday commands, the strictness modes and the basic rules.
Look a topic up here rather than holding the page in context;
the rules to keep in mind are s0ma://guide/survival-card. The
same facts as data, for a program, are
s0ma://guide/quick-reference.json.
resources.name: quick_reference_resource

resources.description:
The s0ma quick reference as data (JSON, schema s0ma-quick-reference@1).

The same facts as s0ma://guide/quick-reference, rendered from the
same value at the same build, so the two cannot disagree: every
kind of declaration with every line it may carry, whether each
must be written and what it may hold instead, the closed sets of
words, the sample project, the commands, the modes, the rules
and the identity of the release described. Read this form when
you want to look a line up by name instead of reading prose.
resources.name: quick_reference_machine_resource

resources.description:
Runtime self-prompting and verified self_inspect wiring.

Shows an application host how to load the content-addressed card and
companion with s0ma-core, register the deterministic self_inspect
adapter, assemble an F1-shaped concierge context profile, and keep
authored intents inside the explicit untrusted-data boundary.
resources.name: self_prompting_resource

resources.description:
The s0ma survival card (under 4 KB) — read this FIRST, hold it in context.

The 60-second version of everything needed to author valid
modules: the bootstrap loop (project_status -> init_project ->
scaffold_module -> edit -> check -> build_project), the three
rules that prevent most errors (only edit .s0ma; a nerve body is
exactly one def; imports are declared in the module header's
requires:, never written in bodies), one minimal valid module,
and the fix for the most common diagnostic codes. Small by
contract — safe to read whole even in a tight context window.
resources.name: survival_card_resource

resources.description:
The s0ma DSL coding-agent system prompt.

A drop-in prompt (or prompt fragment) instructing an LLM how to
author .s0ma files: file structure, declaration types, required
fields, body rules, dependency rules, visibility, naming.
resources.name: system_prompt_resource

resources.description:
The s0ma platform changelog — what's new, per version (FR-MCP-10).

The monorepo's canonical Keep-a-Changelog document covering every
package (s0ma-core, s0ma-dsl, s0ma-mcp — one lockstep version,
INV-4). Read it to learn what changed in the version you are
running, or what an upgrade would bring; pair with
s0ma://meta/version for the installed versions themselves.
resources.name: changelog_resource

resources.description:
The installed s0ma toolchain versions as JSON (FR-MCP-10).

One document answering "what exactly am I talking to":
{server, s0ma_core, s0ma_dsl, s0ma_mcp, s0ma_studi0, mcp_sdk,
python} — the server name and the installed versions of the four
s0ma distributions (s0ma_studi0 is null when the optional viewer
is not installed), the MCP SDK, and the Python runtime, rendered
live via importlib.metadata. Offline by design: no file is read
and no network is touched. Pair with s0ma://meta/changelog to see what
your versions contain.
resources.name: version_resource

resources.description:
The project's operational runbook (O1) as markdown.

The ops-story surface: how to run and health-check the built
application, its declared environment-variable contracts, the
runtime `state_paths` that must NEVER be reverted or regenerated
(the bench's git-revert-of-live-DB failure), the module
inventory, and the ops rules — the same "live state is the
deliverable" rule the survival card carries, restated here with
the state_paths semantics. Rendered from the project resolved
from the server's working directory; when no project (or no
runbook keys) is found it still serves, teaching exactly what to
declare and where. For this project's live runtime facts with an
explicit root, use the project_status tool's `runtime` section.
resources.name: runbook_resource

resources.description:
The authoring server's live self-model (FR-MCP-7) as JSON.

The server eats its own dog food (FR-MCP-11): every tool,
resource, and prompt here is authored as a s0ma component, and
this document is the live graph the served surface is derived
from — components with name, kind, layer, intent, and
dependencies, rendered through s0ma-core's own registry snapshot,
plus the server's name and version. Read it to learn what this
server is and what it can do; the ``describe_server`` tool returns
the same graph with an LLM-ready text rendering.
resources.name: self_model_resource

resources.description:
The current s0ma DSL language specification (normative).

The full grammar and semantics: every declaration kind, field,
namespace rule, strictness mode, error code, and artifact
format. The authority when the guides are not enough.
resources.name: spec_resource

tools.description:
When migrating old Python, record it as interim roster debt.

Example: adopt_file(project_root="/work/app", path="src/legacy.py",
description="Legacy billing adapter") records its intent/hash and
returns mapped/roster counts plus a real scaffold_module action. Never
use this for code you just wrote; new code starts from intent. The
fourth intake reports advisory ADOPTED_CHURN without changing a gate.
Mutating, non-destructive, non-idempotent, and closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: Directory whose pyproject.toml carries the
        [tool.s0ma] table (explicit; never the server's cwd).
    path: File to adopt — absolute, or relative to
        project_root.
    description: Required one-line purpose statement recorded
        with the file. This is authored semantic intent; paths,
        modes, timeouts, and other invocation options keep their
        ordinary required/optional command semantics.
tools.name: adopt_file
tools.title: Record a legacy Python file

tools.description:
After check is clean, build the complete configured project.

Example: build_project(project_root="/work/app", mode="dev") resolves
cross-module edges, writes deterministic artifacts and manifest, and
returns a health_echo for the declared runtime command. It refuses NEW
check errors and hand-edited generated files; overrides are explicit
and separately recorded. Mutating, non-destructive, idempotent, and
closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: Directory whose pyproject.toml carries the
        [tool.s0ma] table (explicit; never the server's cwd).
    mode: Strictness mode — migration, dev, strict, or release.
    clean: Remove cached transpiler output before building.
    force: Overwrite generated .py files even when they were
        edited by hand (discards those edits). Default false —
        the build refuses and reports GENERATED_FILE_DRIFT.
    allow_new_errors: Build even when the edit introduces NEW
        check errors since the last baseline (the override is
        recorded in the build manifest). Default false — the
        build refuses and lists them. Distinct from force (which
        discards hand-edits to generated files).
tools.name: build_project
tools.title: Build the project

tools.description:
After editing intent or code, validate before building.

Example: check(project_root="/work/app", mode="strict") returns
structured findings with owner, owner_intent, and remediation; fix
each finding, then follow next_actions. Add gate_mode="release" only
when the caller intends to evaluate the frozen release policy.
Read-only and closed-world.

Args:
    path: A .s0ma file or directory. Omit to check every
        configured source_roots + test_roots entry of the
        project at project_root.
    project_root: Explicit project root for [tool.s0ma]
        discovery; defaults to the path's own directory.
    mode: Strictness mode (default strict — warnings in dev
        become errors here, matching CI).
    gate_mode: Optional caller-selected evaluation policy
        (migration, dev, strict, or release). When omitted, this
        remains a diagnostic-only check. It is never read from the
        project's authoring mode.
    adoption_policy: Optional explicit path to a
        s0ma-adoption-policy@1 document. Project-local
        adoption_exempt entries classify only and never waive debt.
    expected_adoption_policy_hash: Optional normalized sha256 pin;
        requires adoption_policy and refuses on mismatch.
tools.name: check
tools.title: Check s0ma source

tools.description:
When you do not know which s0ma surface fits, ask the server.

Example: describe_server() returns the live tool name-to-intent map,
situation-to-tool journeys, survival rules, and the server's own
component graph. Choose from this response rather than guessing a tool
or argument name. Read-only and closed-world.
tools.name: describe_server
tools.title: Describe this server

tools.description:
When project_status says false, add the canonical project table.

Example: init_project(project_root="/work/app", mode="dev") appends a
byte-preserving [tool.s0ma] table or creates a minimal pyproject, then
returns survival rules and a project_status action. Repeating it is an
unchanged success. Mutating, non-destructive, idempotent, and
closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: Directory to initialize (explicit root; the
        table is written to <project_root>/pyproject.toml, never
        anywhere else).
    mode: Strictness mode the table declares — migration, dev,
        strict, or release (default dev).
tools.name: init_project
tools.title: Set up a s0ma project

tools.description:
Before grepping for where X is handled, inspect the self-model.

Example: inspect_module(project_root="/work/app", module="billing")
returns canonical tagged IR plus structured depends_on/depended_by
neighbor calls. For roster-only Python it instead returns an exact
DERIVED (unverified) banner and s0ma-derived-surface@1 provenance; that
draft never satisfies a score or gate. Omit module for a survey.
Read-only and closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: The project to query (explicit root).
    module: Module name as declared in its .s0ma header; omit
        for the whole-project survey.
tools.name: inspect_module
tools.title: Inspect the self-model

tools.description:
Ask s0ma one question about s0ma, and get a short answer back.

Example: learn_s0ma(topic="concept:ganglion") returns what a
ganglion is, which release and documentation snapshot the answer
came from, what decided it, the topics to read next, and the page
carrying the full account. A bare term works too ("ganglion"), and
a question this build cannot place comes back with the nearest ids
it does address instead of a guess. Read-only, offline, and the
same question always returns the same answer from the same build.
tools.name: learn_s0ma
tools.title: Ask about s0ma

tools.description:
When legacy extension names remain, preview and apply their migration.

Example: migrate_ext(project_root="/work/app") returns a dry-run plan;
review it, then repeat with dry_run=false and follow the check action.
Collisions abort atomically. Mutating, non-destructive, idempotent, and
closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: The project to migrate (explicit root).
    dry_run: When true (the default), plan only — change nothing.
tools.name: migrate_ext
tools.title: Migrate old file extensions

tools.description:
Write up feedback about s0ma for the user to review — read-only.

Example: prepare_feedback(summary="The remediation was unclear",
category="diagnostic_quality", impact="minor") returns the exact feedback
data and its fingerprint. Nothing is saved or sent; show it, then submit.
tools.name: prepare_feedback
tools.title: Prepare feedback for review

tools.description:
When landing in a tree or diagnosing it, orient in one call.

Example: project_status(project_root="/work/app") returns project and
build posture, mapped/roster module rows and counts, pending semantic
debt, runtime/runbook facts, survival rules, and structured next
actions. With run/health context it also embeds the look-inward-first
diagnostic journey. A non-project is a valid answer pointing to
init_project. Read-only and closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: Directory to orient from (explicit; never
        the server's cwd). Discovery walks upward from here.
tools.name: project_status
tools.title: Project status

tools.description:
When documentation claims behavior, run its executable example.

Example: run_example(project_root="/work/app",
example_name="checkout_happy_path") executes that declaration in a
timeout-bounded subprocess and returns stdout, stderr, duration, and
pass/fail evidence. This executes trusted project code: not read-only,
potentially destructive, non-idempotent, and closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: The project containing the examples.
    example_name: Run only this example (default: run all).
    source_path: Narrow discovery to one file or directory
        (default: the whole project root).
    timeout_seconds: Per-example subprocess timeout.
tools.name: run_example
tools.title: Run a documented example

tools.description:
When starting new behavior, create a valid intent-first component.

Example: scaffold_module(project_root="/work/app",
module_name="billing", kind="SERVICE", layer="APPLICATION") writes a
checked .s0ma skeleton and returns its content, survival rules, and a
check action. Edit intent/contracts rather than generated Python. The
project must already be initialized. Mutating, non-destructive,
idempotent, and closed-world.

Args:
    project_root: The project to scaffold into (explicit root;
        writes outside it are refused).
    module_name: New module name (PascalCase or snake_case).
    kind: Nerve kind — SERVICE, FUNCTION, ADAPTER, or
        ORCHESTRATOR.
    layer: DOMAIN, APPLICATION, INFRASTRUCTURE, or PRESENTATION.
    output_dir: Target directory (default: <project_root>/src),
        inside the project tree.
tools.name: scaffold_module
tools.title: Start a new component

tools.description:
Ask the user to approve this exact feedback data, then send it.

Example: submit_feedback(envelope=..., payload_sha256=...) — pass BOTH
through from prepare_feedback unchanged; any edit needs a fresh one. On
approval this sends and returns a receipt, else it saves a local draft.
tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.title: Send approved feedback

tools.description:
When iterating on one source, emit its Python, IR, and source map.

Example: transpile(source_path="/work/app/src/billing.s0ma",
project_root="/work/app") returns structured diagnostics and emitted
artifact paths. Use build_project for cross-module resolution. Mutating,
non-destructive, idempotent, and closed-world.

Args:
    source_path: A .s0ma file, or a directory of .s0ma files.
    project_root: Explicit project root; defaults to the
        source's own directory. Writes outside it are refused.
    mode: Strictness mode — migration, dev, strict, or release.
    output_dir: Artifact destination (default: next to each
        source file); must be inside the project root.
tools.name: transpile
tools.title: Transpile one source file

annotations.title: Verify imports in the app's Python

tools.description:
After static checks pass, prove imports in the app's real Python.

Example: verify_host(project_root="/work/app",
python="/work/app/.venv/bin/python", gate_mode="release") returns a
nested s0ma-host-verification@1 document with interpreter, dependency,
and isolated import evidence. DANGER: this imports trusted project code
without a sandbox; it may perform arbitrary side effects. Explicitly
approve execution first. Not read-only, potentially destructive,
non-idempotent, and open-world.

Args:
    project_root: Explicit root containing pyproject.toml and build.
    python: Explicit host Python executable. Omit to resolve
        [tool.s0ma].venv_path, then platform .venv, else refuse.
    gate_mode: Optional caller-selected gate policy. Omit for a
        report-only probe whose gate.passes is null.
    module_timeout_seconds: Per-module import timeout.
    timeout_seconds: Whole-run timeout.
tools.name: verify_host
tools.title: Verify imports in the app's Python
